posts.title: Remember the Old Internet?
posts.html:
I’ve been thinking a lot about the old Internet lately.

By the old internet, I mean the one where we used AOL Instant Messenger to stay in touch and share our witty away messages. Where we talked to complete strangers in forums based on common interests. We would pour our deepest thoughts onto LiveJournal or MySpace or Xanga, with our only privacy concern being that our parents might find our posts.

It was a simpler time. In many ways, a better time. The Great Wheel of Capitalism hadn’t quite figured out how to exploit this space for infinite profit. Capturing our attention for hours and hours a day didn’t seem to be anyone’s goal. Tracking screen time would have seemed ludicrous. Things were way more transactional: you paid for a product or closed some pop-up ads and went on your merry way.

I wonder, with the onslaught of AI-generated slop flooding our apps, if we might find a way back to that kind of Internet. When we can’t trust that the content we see in our algorithmic timelines is even real, what’s stopping us from creating spaces where humans can connect with other real humans?

Newsletters are one way to try that, I think. That’s why I’m sending this to you today. Here are some human-made and human-discovered things I found interesting. I hope you do too. But if not, that’s okay. We’re just here on the Internet hanging out. You can click away whenever.

Just like the good old days.

— Russ

🎶 This Week’s Bop 🎶

[Tame Impala - My Old Ways (Official Video) - YouTube]

This song starts off feeling very lo-fi in the traditional sense, as if it were recorded on an old cassette deck. It steps things up quickly, adding layer upon layer until your head can’t stop bopping. It reminds me of the early 2010s without feeling dated. Super catchy and worth a listen. (Warning: melodic f-bombs.)

📰 Something To Read 📰

[The algorithm failed music | The Verge]

Remember music stores and hand-selected employee recommendations? Companies have exploited music discovery to keep us on their platforms, and the algorithm has flattened artists’ ability to sound new and unique.

📺 Something To Watch 📺

[Casually Explained: Gen Z vs Millennials - YouTube]

The two most unfairly hated-on generations and what makes us different from each other. A very funny and insightful eight minute watch.

[The Problem with this Humanoid Robot - YouTube]

Tech companies want us to think the robot revolution is right around the corner. But the products they’re selling today are more fiction than science.

📼 A Touch of Nostalgia 📼

This is what the Apple website looked like in the early 2000s. Check out the new 20GB iPod! And what the heck was an eMac?

📷 Something I Photographed 📷

If you enjoyed this, consider sharing it with someone who might like it. Old school peer-to-peer style. We’re a small group right now and I’d love for us to grow. We’re all we’ve got on this great big Internet after all.

That’s it for this edition. See you next time.
